What does a moving quote include?

Packing, dismantling, transport, reassembly, insurance: what a quote must show, what the rules say, and how to read it before signing.

6 min read · Updated 14 October 2026

Contents

  1. A compulsory, free document
  2. What it should show
  3. The breakdown of services
  4. The fixed price and its exceptions
  5. Insurance and declaration of value
  6. Signing with peace of mind
  7. FAQ

Need tailored advice?

Request a quote

A compulsory, free document

A moving quote is compulsory and free. It must be given to you before any commitment. A phone or online estimate is only an estimate: only the written quote binds the mover. Once signed, the quote and its terms form the contract.

What it should show

  • The company’s details, your identity and address.
  • The planned date or period.
  • Loading and delivery addresses, with access details.
  • The volume to move.
  • The type of transport.
  • The breakdown of services: packing, dismantling, transport, reassembly, unpacking.
  • The price excluding and including tax.

The breakdown of services

This is the part to read carefully. It says who packs fragile and non-fragile items, who dismantles and reassembles furniture, who supplies the boxes, and who unpacks on arrival. At CODEM, this matches the package chosen: see which package to choose. Options are listed too: furniture lift, storage, special items.

The fixed price and its exceptions

The quote must state that the price is final and that no extra charge can be billed, unless the quote is expressly amended. A surcharge remains possible if the client is at fault, for example with inaccurate access information. Hence the value of reporting any change before moving day.

Insurance and declaration of value

When you get the quote, you fill in a declaration of value: it lists items whose value exceeds the per-item compensation cap in the contract. The contract often sets an overall limit and a per-item limit: check them and ask for the declaration if it is not offered.

Signing with peace of mind

If you sign the quote at home, you have a 14-day cooling-off period. Check dates, addresses, volume and services, and ask your questions before signing.

Cody’s tip

Keep the signed quote and the declaration of value with your personal papers on the day, not in a box.

Frequently asked questions

Is the quote charged for?

No, a moving quote is free. At CODEM, the survey is free too.

Is an online quote enough?

It gives an estimate. It relies on what you declare: a volume or access error may then be your responsibility. A survey gives an accurate quote and a fixed price.
